newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shortfall seen in Israel 1997 revenue - minister.
newsitem.headline: Shortfall seen in Israel 1997 revenue - minister.

text.p: Israel's Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Monday that initial estimates indicate government revenue in 1997 will be below target and therefore adjustments will be necessary in next year's budget.
The situation will become more clear once the results of the 1996 budget are available, a ministry statement quoted Meridor as saying during a meeting with Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel.
A revenue shortfall in 1996 has already led to a budget deficit in the first nine months of 8.9 billion shekels, 20 percent more than what was targeted for the entire year.
The statement did not give further details but a source present at the meeting said it was unlikely further cuts to the 1997 budget would be made before January.
Next week the government will submit its plan for a 4.9 billion shekel cut in the 1997 budget, which must be approved by parliament before year's end.
Meridor also told Frenkel that he was considering setting up a mechanism to prevent future deviations from the budget deficit target, the statement said.

He suggested that three times a year -- in April, July and October -- the Finance Ministry examine how the budget is being executed. If a deviation is found, the ministry will make immediate cuts if necessary.
This sort of control will enable the Treasury to remedy problems "in real time", the statement said.
